reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 each MOD argument must be an integer: an arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value (§1989:A.2.2 type 4), so integer items, integer literals, always-integral expressions and integer functions are accepted, and a non-integer literal, a scaled item, a numeric function (§1989:A.2.3) and any expression that does not always yield an integer are refused.

edition-consulted.switches: sig.IntroducedIn (85) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel: MOD is available
ArgPredicate.AppliesAt(edition year) for per-position predicates; MOD's Verified row carries none, so nothing switches

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior|ConstructRegistry over IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs (no hit) and IntrinsicBinder.cs; the type-6 screen (Violation, IntegerViolation, NotAlwaysIntegral) is edition-blind. The floating-point literal 1.0E2 is refused at 85 by the literal's own construct gate, not by this path.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the integer screen is the same code at 85 and 2023 (only the diagnostic text cites §2023 clauses at --std 85)

reader.notes: The accept half and the literal, scaled-item, numeric-function, class and additive-constant refusals are correct at 85. The type-6 expression screen is sound but incomplete by design: a quotient of two items (A / B) and a product with a scaled item (S9V9 * 2) are not refused, and at 85 there is no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking, so the argument is silently truncated. Diagnostics at --std 85 cite §2023 clauses.

reader.known_note: PB1526 (landed) records NotAlwaysIntegral as deliberately sound-not-complete and leaves the static screen fail-open, relying on the runtime EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION test, which COBOL-85 does not have; PB617/PB5208/PB5345 closed sibling shapes. No note claims the item-quotient or scaled-product shape.
